newsitem.title: USA: First Chicago sees lower 97 card profit.
newsitem.headline: First Chicago sees lower 97 card profit.

text.p: First Chicago NBD Corp Executive Vice President Jerry Jurgensen told analysts the company will earn less in its credit card business in 1997 than the $347 million after-tax net income recorded in 1996.
Asked afterward by a reporter how much lower the profit would be this year, he declined to give a specific number.
He told the analysts "we are forecasting a difficult credit environment for the rest of the year" for the card business.
He also told the analysts that First Chicago NBD's card solicitations would rise 17 percent this year from 1996. He said these solicitations would target "less risky" prospects.
Referring to the level of charge-offs in the industry, he said that 1997 would see a higher absolute level than 1996, but the percentage increase should be less than last year.
He said the companies competing in the credit card business are heading into "a huge battle for hanging onto the customers you have."
Jurgensen said that overall, the company's card business' "profitability remains strong despite a difficult credit environment."
